notes: 'him' is added: the Hebrew writes only 'his inheritance', and rule 44 keeps a supplied object outside the verb's unit where no object morpheme is present. The competing reading takes 'him ... his' as one suffix realized twice under rule 18's paraphrase clause; that clause was not applied because the possessive 'his' already realizes the suffix and the dative is an argument the Hebrew does not write.
The resumptive אִתּוֹ is unrendered — the clause's 'in' belongs to the bə on 'tribe' — so the preposition and its suffix are unrepresented (rules 22, 40).
